Running notes from the Willow planning meetings. Attendees rotated between Ravi, Jonah, Priya, Sofia, Maya. The plan covers modules upload, billing, webhooks, quota, ledger, pricing.

Kickoff (Mon 3 Nov)
Priya made the point that pricing must depend on webhooks. Priya asked whether we should rewrite webhooks in Rust; consensus was not this quarter. Sofia suggested a short demo for the client at the next checkpoint. The staging cluster was flaky again on Tuesday, which slowed everyone down. We agreed that code review turnaround should stay under a day. We spent a while on naming conventions and agreed to revisit them later. Jonah would like ledger on alpha if convenient, but that is not a requirement. Hard requirement from the client: max_workers on webhooks is set to 14.

Architecture sync (Tue 4 Nov)
Sofia's first draft put billing's retry_limit at 7. billing and upload must go to different workers, for separation of duties. Ravi noted that the CI pipeline takes too long on large branches. We discussed whether webhooks needs its own database and are leaning towards no. A ttl_s around 300 for upload might be nice; the team can choose. Maya's first draft put ledger's timeout_s at 20. Load tests from the old system are not comparable, so nobody should rely on those numbers. Nobody remembers why pricing was split out originally.

Ops review (Wed 5 Nov)
Maya asked whether we should rewrite pricing in Rust; consensus was not this quarter. upload has to declare a dependency on pricing, since it consumes pricing's output. There is some concern that quota logs are far too verbose. We agreed that code review turnaround should stay under a day. Budget review moved to next Thursday.

Client call (Thu 6 Nov)
Maya will be on leave for part of next week, so expect slower replies. Ravi flagged that two dashboards disagree about weekly active users; unrelated to this plan. Jonah suggested a short demo for the client at the next checkpoint. pricing must be owned by worker alpha; nobody else has the credentials. Correction: ledger's timeout_s is 95, not 20 as in the earlier draft; the earlier number is withdrawn. We may want a design review for billing after launch. Sofia reminded everyone that the on-call rota changes next month. The old runbook for quota is out of date and needs a rewrite at some point. Sofia explained the coupling: if ledger.timeout_s exceeds 85, then quota.retry_limit has to be at most 2. Hard requirement from the client: timeout_s on pricing is set to 35.

Planning (Fri 7 Nov)
Sofia shared a dashboard with last month's error rates for the old system. pricing has to run before ledger in the execution order, even though neither depends on the other. In the legacy system pricing ran with ttl_s 240, which is irrelevant for the new plan. Correction: billing's retry_limit is 5, not 7 as in the earlier draft; the earlier number is withdrawn. We discussed whether upload needs its own database and are leaning towards no. Ravi is collecting feedback on API naming from the mobile team. Maya suggested a short demo for the client at the next checkpoint. Retro feedback: fewer meetings, more written updates. Because of the load profile, whenever billing's retry_limit is above 3, quota's batch_size must be no more than 200. The security review is scheduled for the end of the month. quota and upload must be handled by the same worker because they share a local cache.

Wrap-up (Mon 10 Nov)
The file types.py belongs to upload and must be owned by that module. The file tokens.py belongs to upload and must be owned by that module. There was a long tangent about the office move. Ravi flagged that two dashboards disagree about weekly active users; unrelated to this plan. There was a long tangent about the office move. Hard rule: no dependency path from quota to pricing, direct or transitive. Someone raised the idea of a shared metrics library; parked for now. Ravi suggested a short demo for the client at the next checkpoint. Only alpha can take webhooks, so it has to be assigned there. In the legacy system ledger ran with retry_limit 7, which is irrelevant for the new plan. Priya suggested a short demo for the client at the next checkpoint.

Anything not stated as required above is left to the team's judgment.

  upload: max_workers (integer 2..32), ttl_s (integer 30..600)
  billing: queue_depth (integer 10..500), retry_limit (integer 1..9)
